r1.name: Ministry of Crab
r1.description: Sri Lankan lagoon crab served by size, from the Half Kilo up to the Crabzilla. Housed in the restored Dutch Hospital complex, it is the restaurant most visitors to Colombo are told to book first.

r2.name: Nihonbashi
r2.description: Long-running Japanese kitchen built around Sri Lankan seafood. The sushi counter and the tuna are the reason to come, and the set lunch is the easiest way in.

r3.name: The Gallery Cafe
r3.description: Set in the former offices of the architect Geoffrey Bawa, with a courtyard that stays cool through the afternoon. Worth going for the building alone; the chocolate dessert keeps people coming back.

r4.name: Shanmugas
r4.description: Vegetarian South Indian food served fast and cheap. The lunch rice and curry and the ghee dosa draw a steady queue from midday onward.

r5.name: Upali's by Nawaloka
r5.description: Traditional Sri Lankan cooking presented for a sit-down meal. Good first stop for anyone who wants kottu, hoppers and lamprais in one place without hunting street stalls.

r6.name: Barefoot Garden Cafe
r6.description: Shaded garden cafe attached to the Barefoot bookshop and gallery. Slow lunches, strong coffee, and live jazz on Sunday afternoons.

r7.name: Green Cabin
r7.description: An old Colombo standby for rice and curry, short eats and the lamprais counter. Plain surroundings, consistent food, fair prices.

r8.name: Chinese Dragon Cafe
r8.description: Sri Lankan-Chinese cooking of the kind locals actually order: devilled dishes, fried rice and hot butter cuttlefish, in generous portions.

r9.name: YOUR RESTAURANT
r9.description: Two sentences about what they do well.
